nodes.description: Public string state variable holding the riddle question text.
Address state variable that acts as the owner/authorization anchor.
Bytes32 state variable storing the keccak256 hash of the expected answer and the prize gate.
External payable function that checks the answer hash and value, then pays out the contract balance.
Payable initializer that sets responseHash, question and questionSender only once (responseHash == 0x0).
Payable function restricted to questionSender that drains the whole balance via transfer.
Payable function letting questionSender replace the question and the response hash.
Function letting questionSender transfer ownership to a new address.
Payable fallback function that silently accepts Ether into the contract.
Caller address used for authorization and as the payout recipient.
Origin of the transaction used in Try as an anti-contract check, a phishing/phishing-proxy risk surface.
msg.sender.transfer(this.balance) inside Try, an external value transfer to an attacker-controlled caller.
msg.sender.transfer(this.balance) inside StopGame, an external value transfer that drains the contract.
User-supplied answer string for Try, hashed and compared against responseHash.
Question string supplied to set_game and stored in question.
Answer string supplied to set_game and hashed into responseHash.
Replacement question string supplied to NewQuestion.
Replacement response hash supplied to NewQuestion and written to responseHash.
New owner address supplied to newQuestioner and written to questionSender.

edges.reason: msg.sender is compared against tx.origin inside Try to decide whether the caller may proceed.
tx.origin gates execution inside Try; origin-based authorization is a phishing/access-control weakness.
The user supplied _response is hashed and compared with the stored responseHash.
When the hash matches and value > 3 ether, Try executes the balance transfer to msg.sender.
The external transfer hands control to msg.sender, which can re-enter Try before state is settled.
The first caller of set_game becomes questionSender, taking ownership of the game.
The _response argument of set_game is hashed and written into responseHash.
The _question argument of set_game is written into the question state variable.
msg.sender is stored into questionSender during set_game, defining the authorized account.
StopGame executes a full balance transfer to msg.sender when the caller is questionSender.
The transfer inside StopGame sends control to msg.sender, allowing re-entrant calls into the contract.
StopGame requires msg.sender == questionSender, so the caller value directly controls privileged withdrawal.
NewQuestion only mutates state when msg.sender == questionSender, an owner-gated branch.
The _question argument of NewQuestion overwrites the question state variable.
The _responseHash argument of NewQuestion overwrites the responseHash gate value.
newQuestioner only changes ownership when msg.sender == questionSender.
The newAddress argument of newQuestioner is written into questionSender, transferring ownership.

normalization_plan.reason: Parameter _response only feeds the hash comparison inside Try, so it is merged into the Try function node.
Parameter _question is only used to set the question state var inside set_game, so it is merged into set_game.
Parameter _response is only hashed into responseHash inside set_game, so it is merged into set_game.
Parameter _question only updates the question state var inside NewQuestion, so it is merged into NewQuestion.
Parameter _responseHash only updates responseHash inside NewQuestion, so it is merged into NewQuestion.
Parameter newAddress only assigns questionSender inside newQuestioner, so it is merged into newQuestioner.
